messages.blog.blogPages.aLotOfRemoteAgentProducts: A lot of remote-agent products are marketed around how much control they can give an AI. I wanted to start from the opposite question: how little authority does the AI need in order to finish the job?
messages.blog.blogPages.anAiThatCanOnlyTell: An AI that can only tell you what command to run is safe but limited. An AI that can run every command everywhere is useful but reckless. Remote Arc is built around the space between those two extremes.

Safe access can stay read-only. Developer access can add targeted file edits. Full access can add terminal execution where that is genuinely required.

messages.blog.blogPages.d1StoresTheDurableFactsTh: D1 stores the durable facts that should survive disconnects and deployments: users, paired-device metadata, credential hashes, sessions, OAuth grants, per-device policy, security settings, usage counters and audit metadata. messages.blog.blogPages.forSupportedRemoteArcFile: For supported Remote Arc file mutations, the local agent keeps a bounded undo snapshot on the device itself. The hosted service does not need to become a backup of your file contents in order to give you a recovery path.

messages.blog.blogPages.iDidNotWantRemoteArc: I did not want Remote Arc to be tied to one model vendor. The useful abstraction is not “a ChatGPT remote-control feature” or “a Claude remote-control feature.” It is a set of clearly described tools that compatible AI clients can discover and call. MCP gives Remote Arc that boundary.
messages.blog.blogPages.inAtomicModeTheAgentWrite: In atomic mode the agent writes a temporary file and renames it, without explicitly waiting for storage flushes. Durable mode additionally synchronizes file data, Undo records and directory metadata. On this Intel Mac, L2 Go writes rose from 2.71 ms in atomic mode to 195.80 ms in durable mode. TS showed a similar jump (5.33 to 203.62 ms). Most of that difference is a stronger synchronization policy, not a proof that either language became slower.
messages.blog.blogPages.iSpendALotOfTime: I spend a lot of time using AI tools, and I kept running into the same boundary: the model could explain what I should do, write the command I should run, or generate the patch I should apply — but the final mile was still mine. My files, terminals, repositories and development environments were sitting on real computers, while the AI was trapped behind a chat box.
messages.blog.blogPages.iWantConnectingAnAiTo: I want connecting an AI to your own computer to feel as normal as connecting a calendar or a code repository — but with controls that reflect how much more consequential a computer actually is. Installation should be simple. Permissions should be explicit. The AI client should be replaceable. And the user should always know where the boundary is.
messages.blog.blogPages.l1MeasuresEachExecutionCo: L1 measures each execution core through local JSONL IPC. L2 measures the complete foreground Agent through an authenticated loopback WebSocket relay. Both use matched operations, three alternating rounds, warmup outside the measured set and 600 samples per routine file operation. RSS is sampled after a batch, not peak RAM.
messages.blog.blogPages.l3IsStillOutstandingAForm: L3 is still outstanding: a formal paired TS/Go measurement of ChatGPT/client → production Cloudflare Relay → real device, separating network, routing and execution time. We also need installed-service upgrades, real power/network outages and hardware-specific crash-durability experiments. Benchmark samples are useful engineering evidence, not a blanket performance claim or production SLO.
messages.blog.blogPages.liveDeviceConnectionsAreS: Live device connections are stateful. Durable Objects give Remote Arc a stable place to coordinate WebSockets, track which paired devices are currently reachable and forward a tool call to exactly the selected connection. This avoids trying to force real-time connection state into a stateless Worker request.

messages.blog.blogPages.onceYouExplicitlyEnableUn: Once you explicitly enable unrestricted terminal execution, the shell inherits the permissions of the local operating-system user. Remote Arc can put strong gates around when a terminal tool is available, but it cannot honestly claim that an unrestricted shell is harmless. The right security model is therefore layered control plus explicit user choice, not pretending that powerful execution has no consequences.

messages.blog.blogPages.openclawDescribesItselfAs: OpenClaw describes itself as an open-source AI assistant that runs on your own hardware. Its Gateway owns conversations, channels, agent sessions and integrations. It can connect to chat platforms, host coding or agent runtimes, expose some of its capabilities over MCP, and manage outbound MCP servers for its own runtimes.
messages.blog.blogPages.openclawEmphasizesThatThe: OpenClaw emphasizes that the assistant, state and Gateway can live on hardware you control, with no hosted service in the middle by default. Remote Arc makes a different trade-off: the control plane is hosted so that pairing, OAuth, device discovery and remote routing work without you operating a public Gateway, while actual operating-system execution stays on the paired computer.
messages.blog.blogPages.openclawIsAnAiHomeRemote: OpenClaw is an AI home. Remote Arc is the runtime underneath.
messages.blog.blogPages.openclawUsesMcpInMoreThan: OpenClaw uses MCP in more than one direction. Its documentation describes an MCP server mode for exposing OpenClaw-backed conversations to external clients, and an MCP client-side registry for servers that OpenClaw-managed runtimes may consume. MCP is therefore one part of a wider agent platform rather than the whole product boundary.

messages.blog.blogPages.powerfulRemoteAccessShoul: Powerful remote access should not require a public port, a VPN, or one giant permission switch. The architecture is built around explicit, layered boundaries.

messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcDeliberatelyOwns: Remote Arc deliberately owns a different layer. It does not replace your conversation UI or model; it owns the durable execution layer beneath them: paired computers, task state, checkpoints, bounded Agent Goals, recovery and permissioned tool execution. ChatGPT, Claude, Codex or another compatible MCP client can act as the reasoning source above that runtime.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcIsDeliberatelySp: Remote Arc is deliberately split into a hosted control plane and a local execution plane. That separation is what makes one MCP endpoint work across many AI clients and many computers.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcIsNotABenchmark: Remote Arc is not a benchmark project. Its Agent needs to stay on the computer for hours, preserve one execution owner, reconnect safely and honor file permissions and Undo. Choosing Go was about the shape of that product, not a claim that Go is universally faster than Node.js.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcIsSometimesCompa: Remote Arc is sometimes compared with OpenClaw because both products can ultimately connect AI to a real computer. At a screenshot level the similarity is obvious: an AI asks for something, software on a machine receives the request, and something happens. But that is roughly where the architectural similarity ends.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcIsStillEarlyI: Remote Arc is still early. I am building it in public, using it on my own machines, and refining the product every time something feels more powerful than it feels understandable. That tension is exactly what makes this project interesting to me.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcRecordsOperation: Remote Arc records operational metadata such as which tool ran, which device received it, whether it succeeded and when it happened. The audit design intentionally avoids persisting file contents, raw command arguments, OAuth tokens or raw device credentials.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcSeparatesReadVis: Remote Arc separates read visibility from write authority: ordinary non-sensitive files can be inspected broadly, while persistent mutation is limited to Trusted Write Locations and temporary approvals. Sensitive paths remain separately protected. These controls are not a replacement for operating-system sandboxing, especially once arbitrary terminal execution is enabled.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcThereforeShipsGo: Remote Arc 0.6.0 therefore ships Go as the default native computer Agent: low measured resident memory, native distribution without a Node prerequisite, and one executable that owns the local execution boundary. The TypeScript device runtime was later retired. Cloudflare Worker and Dashboard still use TypeScript.
messages.blog.blogPages.remoteArcThereforeTreatsE: Remote Arc therefore treats every computer as its own trust boundary. A development machine can expose file reads, targeted edits and terminal commands. Another machine can stay effectively read-only. Permissions belong to the device, not to a vague account-wide “agent mode.”

messages.blog.blogPages.thatGapIsWhatPushedMe: That gap is what pushed me to build Remote Arc. The idea sounds simple: let an AI client reach a computer you own. The implementation is not simple at all, because the moment an AI can read files, edit code or run a command, the product stops being a convenience layer and becomes security-sensitive infrastructure.
messages.blog.blogPages.thatIsWhyRemoteArcHas: That is why Remote Arc has an account-level MCP pause, per-device tool policies, revocable OAuth grants, protected paths, local undo support for supported edits and a local execution layer that remains the final authority. None of those controls are glamorous. They are the product.
messages.blog.blogPages.thatMeansOpenclawGivesTec: That means OpenClaw gives technically inclined users more ownership of the assistant platform itself. Remote Arc gives up some of that self-hosting purity in exchange for a simpler connection model across multiple AI clients and multiple computers.
messages.blog.blogPages.theAgentReturnsTheSpecifi: The agent returns the specific tool result through the existing outbound connection. The control plane relays it to the authenticated MCP client. This is why Remote Arc can give an AI useful access to local state without moving the entire development environment into a hosted VM.
messages.blog.blogPages.theConnectionStartsFromTh: The connection starts from the computer you own. Remote Arc does not ask the internet to find an open door into it.
messages.blog.blogPages.theDeploymentPhilosophyIs: The deployment philosophy is almost opposite.
messages.blog.blogPages.theHardestPartIsNotExecut: The hardest part is not execution. It is trust.
messages.blog.blogPages.theHostedControlPlaneNeve: The hosted control plane never directly opens a shell on your computer. The local agent receives an authenticated routed request, checks what it actually exposes and executes the operation through Remote Arc's local execution core. File operations, process inspection, terminal commands and undo all terminate at the machine itself.
messages.blog.blogPages.theHostedSideIsGoodAt: The hosted side is good at identity, discovery, routing, policy and availability. The local side is the only place that should own operating-system execution. Keeping those responsibilities separate makes it possible to improve the hosted experience without pretending that the cloud should become the authority over the user's machine.
messages.blog.blogPages.theImportantLimitationPer: The important limitation: permissions are not magic.
messages.blog.blogPages.theirRelationshipWithMcpI: Their relationship with MCP is different too.
messages.blog.blogPages.theLayeredExperimentKeeps: The layered experiment keeps workspace writes atomic while persisting Undo state more strictly. It lowers some latency, but does not guarantee that the latest workspace edit survives sudden power loss. macOS fsync is not F_FULLFSYNC, and Windows directory synchronization has limits. We will not relabel this as full power-loss protection.
messages.blog.blogPages.theLocalRemoteArcAgentCre: The local Remote Arc agent creates an outbound connection to the hosted relay. That matters to me because I did not want installation to begin with router configuration, firewall exceptions or a machine permanently listening to the public internet. You pair the device explicitly, it receives its own revocable credential, and it can be removed independently later.
messages.blog.blogPages.theLocalRemoteArcAgentEst: The local Remote Arc agent establishes an outbound connection to the hosted control plane. Your router does not need port forwarding, your laptop does not need a public IP, and the machine does not sit on the internet waiting for arbitrary inbound connections.
messages.blog.blogPages.theMcpEndpointIsNotA: The MCP endpoint is not a shared secret pasted into every client. OAuth establishes the user identity, scopes and client grant. Access tokens can be short-lived, refresh tokens can rotate, and a grant can be revoked without changing the paired-device credential.
messages.blog.blogPages.theMostUsefulAiIsNot: The most useful AI is not another chat window. It is an AI that can work with the computer you already have — under permissions you can actually understand and control.
messages.blog.blogPages.theProductShouldMakePower: The product should make powerful actions possible, but it should never make them feel invisible.

Source hashes matter: the Windows follow-up is a different, newer commit than the original baseline. These are not production Cloudflare or ChatGPT end-to-end timings.
messages.blog.blogPages.theTwoModelsCanEvenMeet: The two models can even meet: OpenClaw can consume remote MCP servers, while Remote Arc exposes one. In that setup OpenClaw can be the assistant above Remote Arc, while Remote Arc remains the persistent computer runtime below it. The same runtime can instead be driven by ChatGPT, Claude, Codex or another compatible client.

messages.blog.blogPages.theWorkerHandlesThePublic: The Worker handles the public HTTP surface: MCP requests, OAuth endpoints, pairing APIs, account APIs and the web application. It authenticates the request, checks account state and device policy, applies rate limits and decides whether a call is allowed to proceed.
messages.blog.blogPages.theyCanActuallyComplement: They can actually complement each other.
messages.blog.blogPages.theyCanBothHelpAiAct: They can both help AI act on real computers, but they start from different product boundaries. OpenClaw is an assistant and agent platform; Remote Arc is a persistent runtime that keeps approved work, execution state and real-device access alive beneath the AI client you choose.
messages.blog.blogPages.thisIsWhyIDoNot: This is why I do not think the most useful framing is “which one replaces the other?” If you want a self-hosted personal assistant that owns channels, memory and agent sessions, OpenClaw solves a much broader problem. If you already live in ChatGPT or Claude and mainly want those clients to reach your real computers with explicit device permissions, Remote Arc is intentionally narrower.
messages.blog.blogPages.todayTheSameRemoteArcEndp: Today the same Remote Arc endpoint can be used from ChatGPT, Claude and other compatible clients. The client can change; the paired computers and their permission model do not have to.
messages.blog.blogPages.underTheEarlierF68ab09Nat: Under the earlier f68ab09 native-Go soak, the Mac ran for 7,200 seconds with sampled RSS growing from 14.11 to 17.33 MiB; Windows ran for 7,200 seconds from 17.80 to 24.79 MiB, with a sampled peak of 25.11 MiB. The runs included execution, Undo, conflict checks, managed processes and repeated WebSocket reconnects in an isolated fixture, not a real production outage.

messages.docs.architectureDeepDive.activeToolInpu: Active tool input and output can pass through the hosted Relay and the chosen AI provider. HTTPS/WSS encrypts transport but does not provide zero-knowledge end-to-end encryption. Ordinary audit logs focus on metadata; approved durable Tasks may retain bounded command output or observations.
messages.docs.architectureDeepDive.aDurableTaskIs: A durable Task is a stored contract with a target device, approved plan, optional verification, deadline, iteration budget and explicit trigger. The scheduler acquires a time-bound lease before work; updates check the current lease and monotonically advancing revision. A stale worker must not resurrect cancelled work or overwrite a later checkpoint.
messages.docs.architectureDeepDive.aPermittedCall: A permitted call must pass the AI client's OAuth grant, the account plan ceiling, ownership of the target computer, per-device tool switches, and any local path/sensitive-file rule. Revoking a device and revoking an AI client are separate operations. A previously saved Task never gains new powers merely because a permission was widened later.

messages.docs.architectureDeepDive.arcSupportsBou: Arc supports bounded hosted chat, Tasks, Routines and AI teams Beta; Connect exposes scoped App and device tools, deterministic tasks and enabled experimental goal contracts. D1 records survive independently of either process, but no computer can execute while powered off.

messages.docs.browserModes.fillsAnApiKeyOrToken: Fills an API key or token you enter on a Remote Arc page, once, on the site it was asked for, without your AI seeing it.
messages.docs.browserModes.fillsPasswordsYouSaved: Fills passwords you saved on the computer without your AI seeing them.
messages.docs.browserModes.itIsAFreshAutomatedBro: It is a fresh, automated browser, so some sites (such as the Cloudflare dashboard) show it more human checks. When the Chrome Companion is online, your AI moves such pages to a new tab in your own browser.
messages.docs.browserModes.keepsItsOwnSignInsPer: Keeps its own sign-ins per profile, so you sign in once and later tasks reuse it.
messages.docs.browserModes.letYourAiOpenTabsAnd: Let your AI open tabs and work on the sites you allow in your everyday Chrome, or share the tabs you have open.
messages.docs.browserModes.multiStepWorkClickType: Multi-step work: click, type, choose, upload files and read pages, with real mouse and keyboard input.
messages.docs.browserModes.mustBeInstalledItIsAn: Must be installed. It is an unpacked beta that does not update itself; Dashboard Devices shows when a newer version is out.
messages.docs.browserModes.needsTheComputerAgentC: Needs the computer Agent, Chrome 144 or later and remote debugging turned on.
messages.docs.browserModes.needsTheComputerAgentI: Needs the computer Agent in terminal mode and a Chrome, Edge or Chromium installed.
messages.docs.browserModes.neverFillsPasswordCard: Never fills password, card-number, CAPTCHA or file-picker fields, not even with a one-time secret, so it cannot upload files.
messages.docs.browserModes.opensTabsOnAllowedSite: Opens tabs on allowed sites in a Remote Arc tab group, and keeps a shared tab shared while it stays on its site.
messages.docs.browserModes.pairItThenAllowASite: Pair it, then allow a site once when your AI asks (one Allow button, then Chrome's prompt), share one tab, or share every tab in a window.
messages.docs.browserModes.readsPagesClicksFillsS: Reads pages, clicks, fills, selects, presses keys, scrolls, fills whole forms, navigates and waits for a page.
messages.docs.browserModes.runnerIsTheDefaultAHid: Runner is the default: a hidden task browser with its own sign-ins that never interrupts you. Chrome Companion works through an extension in your own Chrome, signed in as you are. Connecting your running Chrome is an advanced option, used only when you ask. Runner modes require the computer Agent; Chrome Companion pairs separately.
messages.docs.browserModes.sendsOrdersPostsAndOth: Sends orders, posts and other submits once, and keeps a checkpoint so a task can resume in a new conversation.
messages.docs.browserModes.threeWaysToWorkWithYou: Three ways to work with your browser
messages.docs.browserModes.upToTasksAtOnceOn: Up to 4 tasks at once on one computer.
messages.docs.browserModes.useChromeOrLaterInChro: Use Chrome 144 or later. In chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging, enable remote debugging.
messages.docs.browserModes.usesItsOwnSignInsNot: Uses its own sign-ins, not the ones in your everyday Chrome.
messages.docs.browserModes.usesTheSignInsAlreadyI: Uses the sign-ins already in your Chrome.
messages.docs.browserModes.whenAPageNeedsYouA: When a page needs sign-in or verification, the Agent notifies you. The window follows your notification settings and local presence; open the same task window to complete the step yourself.
messages.docs.browserModes.worksSignedInAsYouIn: Works signed in as you, in your own Chrome, with no control banner and no prompt per connection.
messages.docs.browserModes.youCompleteSignInVerif: You complete sign-in, verification codes, CAPTCHAs and payment details yourself.
messages.docs.browserModes.yourAiNeverChoosesItBy: Your AI never chooses it by itself.
messages.docs.browserModes.yourAiUsesRunnerUnless: Your AI uses Runner unless you ask for this. Then a task uses the accounts you are already signed into in Chrome, in its own new window.
messages.docs.browserModes.yourChromeHighlightAll: Chrome asks you to allow each connection
messages.docs.browserModes.yourChromeHighlightOnl: Only when you ask for it

messages.docs.docsPortal.useHostedArcOrBringYour: Use hosted Arc, or bring your own AI through Connect. Choose the guide for the way you work.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.allThreePathsPas: All three paths pass the same authorization and local checks. None of them is an operating-system sandbox: commands that are allowed run as your OS user.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.arcSHostedModelI: Arc's hosted model, inside a Credits budget
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.computersAndTheB: Computers and the browser extension connect outward. There is no inbound port, VPN or desktop stream, and AI clients and computers can each be revoked on their own.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.contractSchedule: Contract, schedule, lease and bounded results
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.encryptedConvers: Encrypted conversation, memory and run history
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.fromAnAiDecision: From an AI decision to an authorized action.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.nothingBeyondThe: Nothing beyond the result and activity
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.operationsUseCon: Operations use connection counts grouped by platform and Agent version, without recording tool payloads. Missing observations do not prove healthy devices.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.remoteArcIsNotRe: Remote Arc is not remote-desktop software, and it is more than an MCP server. The model decides what to do; Remote Arc decides whether it may, routes it to the right account or computer, checks it again where it runs, and records what happened.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theAgentReChecks: The Agent re-checks the permission mode, Trusted Write Locations and sensitive paths. For terminal commands, Safety Guard checks where every delete would land.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theAiClientCalls: The AI client calls the MCP endpoint with an OAuth token scoped to the work it may do.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theAiSeesTheReal: The AI sees the real result and chooses the next step. A lost reply is treated as unknown and inspected, never silently retried.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theApprovedContr: The approved contract; fresh judgment only where configured
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theControlPlaneC: The control plane checks the scope, the account's allowance, device ownership and revocation, and the device's saved tool switches.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theExecutionCore: The Execution Core runs the tool and keeps a Local Undo snapshot for supported edits. Usage and activity are recorded.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.theLifeOfOneTool: The life of one tool call
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.typedOperationsO: Typed operations on your provider accounts
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.yourAccountSDura: Your account's Durable Object forwards the call over the connection your computer opened outward. It keeps no copy of the payload.
messages.docs.docsSystemOverview.yourAiClientTurn: Your AI client, turn by turn
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.aChatCanAuthorizeAn: A chat can authorize and save work that is already concrete: a command, working directory, schedule, event condition, retry bound and verification command. Remote Arc persists that contract and its run state independently of the original chat.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.aDeterministicTaskC: A deterministic task can wait for processes and events without spending model reasoning. But a failed test that needs a new diagnosis, an unexpected repository state, or a choice between new strategies requires an active AI host or the user to resume the work.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.arcStartsABoundedHo: Arc starts a bounded hosted model run for a saved Task or Routine, subject to Credits, time and step limits. Connect can continue a known execution contract after an external chat turn ends, but cannot guarantee that the external AI client will start a fresh reasoning turn. A new strategy needs an active compatible host or a separately configured goal continuation contract.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.arcTasksAndRoutines: Arc Tasks and Routines run bounded hosted AI work using saved instructions, even when the chat tab is closed. Connect Tasks separately persist approved commands, schedules and event conditions. Choose the mode that matches whether the work needs fresh AI judgment or a fixed execution contract.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.chooseArcOrConnectF: Choose Arc or Connect for saved work
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.disconnectsDoNotEra: Disconnects do not erase the task
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.everyExecutionStill: Every execution still checks the paired device, enabled tools, Trusted Write Locations, protected sensitive paths and the saved task permission boundary. Changing the device policy can stop unattended work rather than silently granting new access.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.experimentalSourceG: Experimental source-goal and hosted-goal tools appear only where those capabilities are enabled. They use explicit continuation contracts and still require an available reasoning host. Arc Tasks and Routines use a separate bounded hosted runtime.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.keepAwakeCanHelpASu: Keep-awake can help a supported online computer avoid sleeping during an authorized task. It cannot power on an offline computer.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.repeatTheSameBounde: Run the same saved commands, then a saved check command, and repeat until the check exits with the expected code. Stops after the saved number of attempts or when it expires (24 hours unless set).
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.allModesRunWithoutA: All four modes run without a model. Remote Arc carries out the saved commands on the chosen computer and records each run; the AI client that created the task is not asked again. That is what makes them durable, and also what limits them.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.theVerificationLoop: The fixed verification loop retries the same plan. It does not read why the check failed, so if passing needs a different change, it keeps failing until it reaches its attempt limit or expires. Use it for work that may pass on a later try, such as waiting for a service to become healthy. When each failure needs a new diagnosis, use an Arc Task, or pick the work up again from an active AI client.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.runApprovedDetermin: Run approved commands at a future time, or repeatedly at an interval measured from the end of the previous run.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.startAndTrackOneApp: Start one approved command and keep tracking it after the chat turn ends.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.taskStateIsStoredSe: Task state is stored separately from the live process. If the paired computer is offline, eligible work waits for reconnection. A lost process handle is handled according to the saved recovery policy; Remote Arc does not blindly replay an action whose outcome is unknown.
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.theTaskNeverExpands: The task never expands device authority
messages.docs.longRunningDocs.waitForAConfiguredE: Wait for a configured event, such as a GitHub webhook, then run the approved action.
messages.docs.productDocs.activeFileContentsToolA: Active file contents, tool arguments and command output pass through the hosted relay and your chosen AI client. Transport uses HTTPS/WSS; this is not zero-knowledge end-to-end encryption. Operational audit records retain metadata such as tool, device, time and outcome rather than raw payloads.
messages.docs.productDocs.addRemoteArcToACompatib: Add Remote Arc to a compatible AI client, sign in and choose what it can access. This reference covers authorization, app actions, device tools and browser sharing.
messages.docs.productDocs.advancedAndOptionalYour: Advanced and optional. Your AI uses Runner unless you ask it to use your own Chrome: in this mode Chrome asks you to click Allow for every new connection and shows a control banner, which can interrupt what you are doing.
messages.docs.productDocs.allConnectToolCapabilit: All Connect tool capabilities are available on every plan, including binary reads, temporary file links, background commands, schedules, condition watches, source-controlled Agent Goals and supported keep-awake. Free retains 10,000 tool calls per month; when they run out, a one-time 7-day unlimited Connect trial starts automatically, then calls continue at 2 per minute until the monthly reset. Free also includes 2 GB of binary transfer per month, shared by binary reads and file link downloads; paid plans have no transfer limit. Account authorization and device permissions still apply; hosted model access and third-party charges are separate. Check Settings → Plan & usage for your current allowance.
messages.docs.productDocs.allowedSitesApplyToBoth: Allowed sites apply to both Runner modes. Embedded forms on other sites also need to be named. Complete sign-in, verification codes and CAPTCHAs in the task browser yourself, then resume the same task. Browser authentication automation is disabled, and saved approvals cannot enable it. Payment details also need you. Review answers before authorizing a final submission.
messages.docs.productDocs.anAiClientSOwnSandbox: An AI client's own sandbox protects its execution environment; it does not automatically contain commands sent through MCP to your computer. For constrained file-only work, keep terminal disabled. For stronger isolation now, pair a dedicated restricted OS account or an isolated machine you manage. A container or VM requires its own correctly configured boundary.
messages.docs.productDocs.aOneMinuteCloudSchedule: A one-minute cloud scheduler advances due Tasks with persisted leases and revisions. Saving a Task is not evidence that it ran; Dashboard shows actual run state, results and scheduler health separately.
messages.docs.productDocs.aProcessHandleAndADurab: A process handle and a durable Task have different lifetimes
messages.docs.productDocs.arcAdditionallyStoresEn: Arc additionally stores encrypted chat messages, tool observations, selected Skills and bounded personal memories for hosted work. Relevant context is sent to the selected model provider. Inspect or delete personal notes in Memory settings; chat history, App accounts and device access have separate controls.
messages.docs.productDocs.arcTasksAndRoutinesRunB: Arc Tasks and Routines run bounded hosted AI work using your trial or paid Arc Credits, even when its chat tab is closed. Connect Tasks save approved deterministic commands, schedules and condition watches; new AI decisions still need a compatible active host. Computer work requires an online Agent and device permissions; cloud App work does not need a paired computer. A UI preview uses simulated data.
messages.docs.productDocs.aSelectableIsolatedExec: A selectable isolated execution profile is a future design, not a working Dashboard feature. Native access remains useful for your existing projects and tools. The engineering decision explains when isolation is appropriate and what must be verified before adding an isolation switch.
messages.docs.productDocs.askForWorkInTheChat: Ask for work in the chat you already use and name the target computer. Reading a file, inspecting a process or running a short command is an ordinary tool call. It does not create a Task for every operation.
messages.docs.productDocs.aTaskIsASavedUnit: A Task is a saved unit of ongoing work: its goal or fixed plan, trigger, device, approved capabilities, deadline and progress. It can contain many tool calls. When you request ongoing or scheduled work, the AI can save that Task inside your authorization; you do not need to fill out a Dashboard form. Dashboard is there to inspect results, pause or cancel tasks and change device permissions.
messages.docs.productDocs.backgroundServiceContro: Background-service controls and power leases are internal device/Dashboard helpers; local MCP additionally exposes directory browsing, Undo lists and managed-process lists. MCP event methods are protocol extensions, not additional tools.
messages.docs.productDocs.backgroundWorkSchedulin: Background work, scheduling, adaptive goals, source-agent continuation and task keep-awake, each with its own switch.
messages.docs.productDocs.beforeATerminalCommandR: Before a terminal command runs, resolves where each delete would land and refuses drive roots, home and personal folders, system and credential folders, the Undo store and targets it cannot resolve unambiguously. Defense in depth, not an OS sandbox.
messages.docs.productDocs.callDeviceToolsForTheTo: Call device_tools for the tools available on that computer.
messages.docs.productDocs.callListDevicesAndResol: Call list_devices and resolve the user-named computer to device_id.
messages.docs.productDocs.claudeUsesACustomRemote: Claude uses a custom Remote MCP connector and OAuth. Cursor can use the generated MCP installation link or its remote server configuration. Other clients must support the endpoint transport and OAuth discovery; compatibility does not imply they can continue an agent overnight.
messages.docs.productDocs.connectAnAvailableAppIn: Connect an available app in your workspace's Apps page. In Arc, ask to use that account for a specific result. Supported MCP connections expose the fixed catalog through three tools: list_apps lists your connected accounts and searches actions by use_case, run_app_read_action runs one read-only action and run_app_write_action runs one change you asked for. Every action ID is listed in those two tools' schemas, and list_apps returns an action's exact arguments. These tools are still under review for the public ChatGPT plugin and may not yet be available through that listing.
messages.docs.productDocs.connectCannotPromiseToW: Connect cannot promise to wake the same external chat for a new reasoning turn. Experimental source-goal and hosted-goal tools appear only when enabled and use explicit continuation contracts; they do not provide unlimited reasoning or override permissions and budgets.
messages.docs.productDocs.connectKeepsDeterminist: Connect keeps deterministic commands and waits durable without continuous model inference. A new diagnosis or strategy needs an active compatible host. Arc Tasks and Routines separately start bounded hosted model runs using saved instructions and account Credits.
messages.docs.productDocs.connectTheAiClientToThi: Connect the AI client to this endpoint and complete Remote Arc OAuth. Use the client-specific installation guide for ChatGPT, Claude or Cursor. Pairing a computer and authorizing an AI client are independent: you can revoke either relationship separately.
messages.docs.productDocs.connectTheChromeYouAlre: Connect the Chrome you already use
messages.docs.productDocs.connectUsingTheClientIn: Connect using the client installation path
messages.docs.productDocs.credentialAndBrowserPro: Credential and browser-profile paths, with narrow explicit exceptions.
messages.docs.productDocs.deviceOfflineCheckPower: Device offline: check power, login, local agent and network. Reconnect can resume a saved Task; the relay cannot wake a powered-off machine.
messages.docs.productDocs.downloadAndUnzipTheComp: Download and unzip the companion. In chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, choose Load unpacked and select the extracted folder. Open its popup, select Connect to Remote Arc and approve browser pairing. Then allow a site once when your AI asks (or from the popup), or explicitly Share this tab. It is an unpacked beta, not a Chrome Web Store extension; downloaded versions must be reloaded manually.
messages.docs.productDocs.durableDeterministicTas: Durable deterministic Tasks support a future ISO timestamp or interval schedule. Recurring runs of the same task do not overlap, and the next interval starts from the previous run's completion. These Connect contracts do not add calendar cron or missed-run backfill. Arc Routines separately support local-time schedules with IANA timezones and DST handling.
messages.docs.productDocs.durableTasksSaveExecuti: Durable tasks save execution, not an immortal AI
messages.docs.productDocs.durableTaskStorageIsSep: Durable task storage is separate from audit storage. It saves approved commands/plans, objectives, verification, policy snapshots, run summaries, factual memory, bounded observations and completion evidence. Observations can contain file content or command output. Pending source decisions can contain edit content; their bodies are cleared after consumption, while idempotency hashes remain.
messages.docs.productDocs.enableBrowserRunnerForT: Enable Browser Runner for the computer in Dashboard and keep its Agent running. The default Runner uses a separate browser profile and keeps its window in the background. After submission or navigation, the Agent checks for sign-in and verification blockers and notifies you. Window presentation follows your notification preferences and local presence; scheduled and routed Arc runs use notifications only. Open the existing task window, complete authentication yourself, then resume the same task_id. The owner-only live view shows the task viewport while you are watching; it does not provide remote input. Choose one profile per person, sign in once, and reuse that profile in later tasks and chats. Sign-ins entered in its window are saved locally unless browserRunnerSaveLogins is disabled. You can also add a site-bound sign-in with remotelink vault add on the computer. fill_secret fills it only on its saved sites; the password stays out of the AI conversation.
messages.docs.productDocs.fileReadsAndWritesAreIn: File reads and writes are independent. The local core resolves paths, including symlinks, before enforcing workspace roots and sensitive-path protection. You can allow one required credential file without disabling all sensitive-path protection.
messages.docs.productDocs.filesProtectedPathsAndL: Files, protected paths and Local Undo
messages.docs.productDocs.finishedWithoutIndepend: Finished without independent verification: provide a reliable verification command next time. A completion label alone is not an independent test.
messages.docs.productDocs.forAKnownAcknowledgedPr: For a known, acknowledged process whose handle is lost, a deterministic Task can restart the attempt or fail, according to recovery. Restart creates a new attempt; it does not revive the same PID. Agent Goals inspect the current state before choosing another action. If dispatch happened without an acknowledged result, the system records uncertainty and avoids blindly replaying the effect.
messages.docs.productDocs.freshAiJudgmentHasAHard: Fresh AI judgment has a hard boundary
messages.docs.productDocs.futureStartsRecurringWo: Future starts, recurring work and keeping the computer awake
messages.docs.productDocs.hostedGoalsSendBoundedC: Hosted goals send bounded context to the configured planner provider. Source goals return it to the authorized source client. Task event callbacks use an encrypted stored signing secret and carry short change metadata; readers obtain full context through authorized tools. Full local process capture and Undo snapshots have local retention limits.
messages.docs.productDocs.ifChromeIsWaitingForAll: If Chrome is waiting for Allow, retry the same task_id after approving; the pending request lasts 3 minutes. Closing a task closes its own tab. The connection disconnects 5 minutes after the last task detaches; unused tasks pause after 20 minutes. Stopping the Agent disconnects and leaves task windows for later recovery. If already disconnected, closing a task reports tab_left_open so you can close that window manually. Your other tabs and Chrome profile are kept.
messages.docs.productDocs.inChatgptInstallThePubl: In ChatGPT, install the published Remote Arc plugin and connect your account. Other compatible clients can add the HTTPS endpoint through their remote MCP settings. To use computer tools, also install the local Agent and pair that computer to the same Remote Arc account. The public ChatGPT plugin's connected-App tools are still under review; Arc and supported custom MCP connections retain their App integrations.
messages.docs.productDocs.itsHandleAndCapturedOut: Its handle and captured output are in the running agent's memory. They are lost on agent restart; a machine reboot ends the old OS process.
messages.docs.productDocs.listProcessesInspectsOs: list_processes inspects OS processes without granting shell execution. start_process requires terminal permission and can run synchronously or in background mode. Background mode returns process_id; process_status, process_output and stop_process use that local agent handle.
messages.docs.productDocs.nativeDownloadsHomebrew: Native downloads, Homebrew, upgrades and stopping the Agent
messages.docs.productDocs.needsFreshAiJudgmentThe: Needs fresh AI judgment: the deterministic Task should stop or wait. Resume it from an active supported AI host rather than pretending the original Chat is still running.
messages.docs.productDocs.newDevicesStartWithRead: New devices start with read-oriented tools. File editing, terminal execution, workspace roots and login background connection are separate choices. Finish setup before connecting your AI. The background switch installs an OS login service only after setup, and Dashboard reports its verified local state.
messages.docs.productDocs.noPublicInboundPortRout: No public inbound port, router forwarding or VPN is required. Persistence is handled by the task scheduler and database; the device connection provides execution when the computer is available.
messages.docs.productDocs.npxRemotelinkSafeKeepsA: npx remotelink --safe keeps a local read-only ceiling that Dashboard cannot expand.
messages.docs.productDocs.oauthAndDeviceAccessAre: OAuth and device access are separate
messages.docs.productDocs.oneConnectionForYourApp: One connection for your apps and computers.
messages.docs.productDocs.onTheWindowsMacosOrLinu: On the Windows, macOS or Linux computer that owns the project, install the native Agent using a download, Homebrew or npm/npx. Only the npm/npx command below requires Node.js 20 or newer. The Agent opens a short-lived browser pairing flow. Sign in, compare the code and approve the correct machine.
messages.docs.productDocs.openChromeOrLaterOnThe: Open Chrome 144 or later on the linked computer. Visit chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging and enable Allow remote debugging for this browser instance.
messages.docs.productDocs.openTheChromeCompanionD: Open the Chrome Companion download and installation page
messages.docs.productDocs.pairAComputerChooseItsP: Pair a computer, choose its permissions and connect your AI through Remote MCP. Use ordinary tools for immediate work, or a durable Task when work needs to continue, wait for an event or run later.
messages.docs.productDocs.passDeviceIdWithDeviceT: Pass device_id with device tool calls; check the workspace and action's permission before a write or command.
messages.docs.productDocs.pathSyntaxIsTheTargetCo: Path syntax is the target computer's syntax. Ordinary calls need an online device. A saved Task can wait for reconnection; that does not make a direct call durable.
messages.docs.productDocs.persistentRootsWhereFil: Persistent roots where file mutation can happen without per-request approval; scoped terminal commands also require an in-scope cwd.
messages.docs.productDocs.policyChangedOrResultUn: Policy changed or result unknown: read the error and journal, inspect the actual state, then choose a safe next step. Do not repeat an uncertain external effect blindly.
messages.docs.productDocs.readEditTerminalAndBrow: Read, edit, terminal and browser capabilities. Read-only, Developer and Full are convenience presets; individual tools remain controllable.
messages.docs.productDocs.readTheTabsYouExplicitl: Read the tabs you explicitly share
messages.docs.productDocs.remoteArcDoesNotProvide: Remote Arc does not provide GUI desktop control, arbitrary shell containment, exactly-once external effects or guaranteed model reasoning duration. Set a deliverable, verification and reasonable limits; treat failed, expired, cancelled and blocked work as distinct outcomes.
messages.docs.productDocs.remoteMcpExposesAuthori: Remote MCP exposes authorized App and device tools. Connect persists deterministic task contracts, with experimental goal tools where enabled. Arc provides bounded hosted chat, Tasks, Routines and AI teams Beta on the same account connections. Availability still depends on configuration, access, device version and Credits.
messages.docs.productDocs.repeatTheSameBoundedWor: Repeat the same saved commands and check command until the check exits with the expected code, the attempt limit is reached or the task expires. It does not diagnose a failure or change approach.
messages.docs.productDocs.reuseTheSameRequestidWh: Reuse the same requestId when checking a request after a timeout. If the result is unknown, inspect it before starting another write. Reconnect an account if permissions are missing or authorization has expired. Some app operations use a separately billed provider API account.
messages.docs.productDocs.runApprovedDeterministi: Run approved deterministic work later or at a completion-based interval.
messages.docs.productDocs.runnerSignInOnceReuseYo: Runner: sign in once, reuse your profile
messages.docs.productDocs.sandboxIsolationWouldPl: Sandbox isolation would place commands in an OS-enforced environment with restricted files, processes, credentials and network access. Remote Arc currently executes as the local OS user. Tool permissions, workspace paths and Safety Guard reduce reach and mistakes, but do not create an OS sandbox. A shell can reference paths beyond cwd and use the local user's network access.
messages.docs.productDocs.searchAllToolsAppOperat: Search all tools, App operations and parameters
messages.docs.productDocs.setUpTheComputerAndThe: Set up the computer and the AI client once
messages.docs.productDocs.startAndTrackOneKnownCo: Start and track one known command after the chat turn ends.
messages.docs.productDocs.startTheTaskWithBrowser: Start the task with browser=your_chrome. Leave profile and headless out. Chrome asks you to click Allow for the connection.
messages.docs.productDocs.supportedWriteFileAndEd: Supported write_file and edit_block edits can save the previous file state under ~/.remotearc/undo. Snapshots stay on the computer. Undo checks the current file hash before restoring, so a newer change is not silently overwritten. Shell edits, deployments, database changes and external API actions are outside Local Undo.
messages.docs.productDocs.taskKeepAwakeRequiresBo: Task keep-awake requires both device permission and keep_awake=true on that task, plus a compatible local agent. Active tasks renew short-lived OS power requests; completion, cancellation, pause or lease expiry releases them. This does not power on a shut-down computer, defeat forced sleep or permanently change power settings. Future tasks need an available computer when they start.
messages.docs.productDocs.taskPermissionIsPersist: Task permission is persistent authority for the saved work. Every future device action still checks ownership, revocation, approved tools and the local path policy. Account MCP Pause blocks AI client requests but does not disconnect device Agents or terminate independently running tasks. Device Pause shuts down the execution Core while preserving only an authenticated wake connection; Resume restores execution. Disconnect Completely closes both connections and disables remote waking.
messages.docs.productDocs.taskPermissionsDoNotGra: Task permissions do not grant missing file or terminal tools. Source continuation and task keep-awake require opt-in. Turning off a task permission cancels affected active tasks. Changing the frozen device tool/path policy stops unattended work; it does not grant an old Task new authority.
messages.docs.productDocs.theAiClientSAccountLeve: The AI client's account-level authorization. Device policy still applies.
messages.docs.productDocs.theChromeCompanionAddsS: The Chrome companion adds scoped page context to the same MCP connection. Share as many tabs as you need; Remote Arc has no fixed tab-count cap, and every tab starts read-only. You can separately enable Click & fill for one shared tab. Interaction requires a fresh page snapshot, rejects stale element refs, and blocks recognized password, payment-card and file-picker fields. Complete sign-in, verification codes and CAPTCHAs in your browser yourself, then your AI can continue. Public MCP calls cannot automate these authentication steps. Browser tools remain ordinary scoped MCP tools; durable deterministic Tasks do not gain extra browser authority.
messages.docs.productDocs.theCurrentNativeAgentSe: The current native Agent separates process recovery from Relay reconnect. Normal launches keep the terminal open. macOS launchd/Linux systemd supervise a daemon; Windows login starts a hidden supervisor that restarts its Agent. One Agent executes while other terminals show its operation log. Recovery off preserves execution; Stop background Agent is separate. Windows needs its supervisor to remain running. Sleep and power loss still make the computer unavailable. Update all running instances to use the execution lease.
messages.docs.productDocs.theEndpointUsesOauthAut: The endpoint uses OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE and published discovery metadata. Sign in to Remote Arc and review the requested scopes. Device credentials stay with the local agent; you do not paste a computer credential into the AI client. Revoking a client grant, pausing account MCP access or revoking a device can stop access independently.
messages.docs.productDocs.theGroupsBelowCoverMcpT: The groups below cover {toolCount} MCP tools for devices, saved work and connected apps. Your client shows the tools enabled for your account. Computer tools also depend on the selected device's permissions and installed Agent. process_status and process_output require computer:write. App tools use list_apps to find an action and its arguments, then run_app_read_action or run_app_write_action to run it in a linked account; they do not require a paired computer.
messages.docs.productDocs.theInstallerVerifiesSha: The installer verifies SHA256 and installs to ~/.local/bin without sudo. Upgrades, runs without a terminal and REMOTEARC_NO_START=1 only install; then start the Agent with remotelink, or the full path the installer prints if that directory is outside PATH. Set REMOTEARC_INSTALL_DIR to an absolute directory to choose another location. Stop the Agent before rerunning the installer to upgrade.
messages.docs.productDocs.theLocalExecutionPlaneI: The local execution plane is Go: apps/agent contains pairing, Relay sessions, process recovery and journals; packages/execution-core is an independent Go module for file/process tools, local policy and Undo. They compile into one native executable. The npm CLI only installs and launches it. TypeScript remains in the cloud Relay, Dashboard and shared wire contracts.
messages.docs.productDocs.theSavedContractProgres: The saved contract, progress and run history remain in D1. After device reconnection, execution continues from the saved state according to the recovery policy.
messages.docs.productDocs.theTaskOpensItsOwnWindo: The task opens its own window using your current sign-ins. Several tasks share the connection. A new connection needs Allow again; Chrome shows a control banner while connected.
messages.docs.productDocs.theWorkerAuthenticatesT: The Worker authenticates the account and client, checks policy and selects the device. Per-user Durable Objects route live requests over the device's outbound WebSocket. D1 stores accounts, authorization, policies and durable task progress. Commands and file operations execute on the paired computer using its installed software.
messages.docs.productDocs.toolUnavailableInspectD: Tool unavailable: inspect device_tools, device policy and the local --safe ceiling. A Task switch alone does not enable terminal access.
messages.docs.productDocs.useADurableLongTaskFor: Use a durable long_task for a lengthy build, export or script. Use launchd, systemd or Windows Services when the workload is a permanent service. These choices solve different lifecycle needs.
messages.docs.productDocs.useADurableTaskWhenThe: Use a durable Task when the work is already concrete: an approved command, working directory, trigger, retry bound and optional verification command. Remote Arc persists that contract and run state independently of the chat that created it.
messages.docs.productDocs.useAServiceManagerForA: Use a service manager for a daemon that must be restarted and supervised independently of an AI Task.
messages.docs.productDocs.useSharedTabListToSelec: Use shared_tab_list to select tab_id when several tabs are shared. shared_tab_read returns the page with a snapshotId plus stable refs for that snapshot, and can also return the selected text, links or one table. shared_tab_click and shared_tab_fill require both that snapshot and an explicit per-tab Click & fill grant; a click invalidates the snapshot and the page must be read again. messages.marketing.marketingPages.addsTerminalCom: Adds terminal commands and background processes. Commands can change things Local Undo cannot reverse, so you confirm before turning it on.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.addTheRemoteArc: Add the Remote Arc endpoint to Claude and complete OAuth. Claude connects to a hosted MCP server while the paired device remains a separate execution boundary.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.aDurableAutomat: A durable automation may execute hours after the MCP request that created it has ended. Deterministic automations therefore store an explicit trigger and action plan. Adaptive Agent Goals store a user-approved objective, success criteria, tool set, optional deterministic verification, iteration/expiry limits, target device and permission snapshot. The planner can reinterpret results and choose a different next action, but cannot expand those stored authority boundaries.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.anAccountWideMc: An account-wide MCP pause blocks authenticated MCP calls server-side until the user resumes them. Individual OAuth grants can be revoked without re-pairing computers. Individual device credentials can be revoked, forcing that machine to pair again. Stopping the local agent also removes the machine from live routing because the connection is outbound from the device.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.aNewlyPairedCom: A newly paired computer starts in Safe, which is read-only. Choose a preset on the computer's page in the dashboard, or switch individual skills on and off. Your AI client's authorization never goes beyond these settings.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.askForEditingAn: Ask for editing and terminal tools; the computer's own permissions decide whether they are available.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.beforeSupported: Before supported write_file and edit_block changes, Remote Arc can save the previous state under ~/.remotearc/undo. Snapshot contents stay on the paired computer. A restore checks the post-edit file hash first; if the file changed again, automatic restore is refused rather than overwriting newer work.

messages.marketing.marketingPages.chooseTheGuideF: Choose the guide for the AI client you use. messages.marketing.marketingPages.conditionWatchC: Condition Watch callback URLs contain a high-entropy secret and act as bearer capabilities. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored and delivery IDs can be deduplicated when supplied. A configured GitHub condition can merge one explicitly selected pull request with a repository-scoped GitHub App installation token. The current webhook transport still relies on the secret callback URL rather than claiming provider-specific GitHub HMAC verification.

messages.marketing.marketingPages.dashboardAuthen: Dashboard authentication, MCP client authorization and device pairing are separate credentials. AI clients use OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE. A paired computer receives its own revocable device credential; the hosted database stores a SHA-256 hash rather than the raw credential.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.directProcessHa: Direct process handles are local to the agent. Durable Tasks preserve progress across interruptions; recovery may inspect or start a new attempt rather than preserve the same OS process.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.discoverConnect: Discover connected apps and read data within each account's granted access.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.doesRemoteArcEx: Does Remote Arc expose a port on my computer?
messages.marketing.marketingPages.doIHaveToUseOnl: Do I have to use only ChatGPT?
messages.marketing.marketingPages.downloadTheNati: Download the native Agent for the computer you want your AI to use. No Node.js is needed. Run it, approve browser pairing with the same Remote Arc account, and keep the computer online. If already paired, start the existing Agent instead of installing again.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.durableGoalsSto: Durable goals store their contract, bounded observations, factual memory and completion evidence separately from the operational audit. Observations may contain file contents or command output. Source decisions are scoped to the account/client and fenced by revision. Signed task events require a verified callback and secure egress; cloud GitHub actions also require explicit account/repository permission.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.durableTaskReco: Durable task recovery is separate: the control plane saves contracts, checkpoints and run history. After an interruption it checks leases, revisions and actual device state before continuing. It preserves work progress rather than guaranteeing that the same local process survives a restart.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.eachPairedCompu: Each paired computer connects outward to the control plane and receives only routed calls for the device selected by the AI workflow.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.encryptionInTra: Encryption in transit is not the same thing as end-to-end zero knowledge. To route a read_file response or process_output result, the hosted relay must process that active payload. Remote Arc therefore makes a narrower storage claim: operational audit records are designed around device, tool, result state and time, rather than intentionally persisting file contents, raw command arguments or tool results.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.everyFutureDevi: Every future device action still passes the normal ownership, revocation, allowed-tool and local path-policy checks. Unattended tasks do not enter a mid-run approval queue: disconnects wait for the device, known acknowledged deterministic attempts use the configured restart/fail policy when a handle is lost; unknown dispatch effects are not blindly replayed, and Agent Goals re-inspect state before choosing another action after a lost process handle. If the device security policy itself changes, execution stops and records the policy change instead of waiting for someone to approve it.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.existingPathAnc: Existing path ancestors are canonicalized on the device before execution. The goal is to prevent an apparently allowed path from trivially escaping through a symlink. When a protected project genuinely needs one sensitive file or directory, a narrow exception can be added instead of disabling protection globally.

messages.marketing.marketingPages.readFilesEditSu: Read files, edit supported content, inspect processes, run approved commands, share browser-tab context or keep a device read-only depending on its policy.

messages.marketing.marketingPages.readOnlyToolsMa: Read-only tools may inspect ordinary non-sensitive files outside Trusted Write Locations. File mutation outside those locations requires approval. messages.marketing.marketingPages.remoteArcAllows: Remote Arc allows an AI client to act on a real computer. The useful question is therefore not whether the system is 'secure' in the abstract, but which component is trusted for which decision, what the hosted service can observe, and how access can be constrained or revoked.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.remoteArcAssume: Remote Arc assumes the paired computer and its operating-system account are under the user's control. It also assumes that granting terminal execution is materially more powerful than granting read-only file or process inspection. The design therefore tries to keep those capabilities separable instead of treating 'computer access' as one permission.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.remoteArcConnec: Remote Arc connects ChatGPT to Windows, macOS and Linux through an OAuth-protected Remote MCP endpoint and an outbound-only device connection.
Remote Arc connects Claude to explicitly paired Windows, macOS and Linux computers while keeping operating-system execution on the device you control.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.remoteArcIsAHos: Remote Arc is a hosted Remote MCP bridge that lets compatible AI clients discover and invoke approved capabilities on Windows, macOS and Linux computers you pair.

messages.marketing.marketingPages.safeDeveloperAn: Safe, Developer and Full are convenience presets over the same editable per-device skill list. Reading files can remain enabled while editing is off. Process listing can remain enabled while start_process is off. Terminal access, when enabled, is real shell execution under the local OS user's permissions.
messages.marketing.marketingPages.safetyGuardIsDe: Safety Guard is defense in depth. Before a shell command runs, it resolves where each delete would land, including rd, del, Remove-Item, rm, find -delete, robocopy /MIR, rsync --delete and inline rmtree or rmSync calls, through nested cmd, PowerShell and sh layers, variables, wildcards and simple pipelines. It refuses drive and volume roots, home and personal folders, system directories, credential stores and the Remote Arc Undo store, and any delete whose target it cannot resolve unambiguously, such as escaped quotes across nested shells, unset variables or command substitution. Narrow cleanup such as node_modules, %TEMP% or Library/Caches still runs. It also blocks a few other catastrophic commands such as disk formatting and shutdown. It is not an operating-system sandbox: a script can still compute paths at run time, so it does not replace running the agent under an appropriately restricted local user.

messages.marketing.trustPages.aiClientsConnectedA: AI clients, connected apps, model providers and payment processors have their own terms, account requirements and availability. Connect does not include a subscription to your chosen AI client. Some app actions use credits or incur charges in your own provider account, such as media generation or messaging; Remote Arc usage allowances do not cover those charges unless expressly stated. Not every listed tool is available to every provider account or region.
messages.marketing.trustPages.aiOutputAndToolExec: AI output and tool execution can be incomplete or incorrect. Check important results before relying on them. Tasks and routines can continue after you close a chat, subject to their limits and enabled connections. A device must be online and available for local execution. Cloud coordination does not make an offline computer available, and we do not guarantee an outcome or uninterrupted 24/7 execution.
messages.marketing.trustPages.arcCanKeepEncrypted: Arc can keep encrypted, bounded personal facts and recent work summaries separately from chat history. It retrieves a small relevant selection for later conversations; device availability is checked from current connection records. Memory is limited to 100 facts and 40 work summaries, rather than a copy of all files and device content. In Settings → Memory you can inspect, edit and delete saved facts, remove summaries, clear all memory, or switch it off. Clearing memory also prevents earlier in-flight runs from saving it again. Clearing memory does not delete chat history or recall data already sent to model providers. Deleted chats become eligible for a scheduled content purge after 24 hours and their execution deadlines; payment and usage identifiers are retained separately.
messages.marketing.trustPages.aSetupQuestionSomet: A setup question, something unexpected, or an idea for what comes next. We’re here to help.
messages.marketing.trustPages.aTrialWhenOfferedSt: A trial, when offered, starts only when you explicitly activate it and ends at its stated time or allowance. It does not automatically become a paid subscription. Model choice and token usage determine how quickly Credits are consumed; tool calls, devices, concurrency and execution time can have separate limits. Remaining trial Credits are retained after the trial ends. Monthly Credits expire with their billing period. Purchased top-up Credits do not expire, but require an active paid plan to use. Credits are service usage units, not cash or a transferable balance. There are no automatic overage purchases. See the current plan and usage details in Billing before purchasing.
messages.marketing.trustPages.connectingAnAppAuth: Connecting an app authorizes Remote Arc to use the permissions granted by that provider. We store connection identity, granted scopes, connection status and encrypted access or refresh credentials needed to make authorized requests. Available read and write tools are enabled for the connection within those scopes. App requests and results pass between Remote Arc, the provider, and the AI client or Arc session using the tool. App call arguments and results are stored encrypted to track execution and prevent duplicate actions. Disconnect an app in your workspace to revoke its Remote Arc connection; you can also revoke access at the provider.
messages.marketing.trustPages.connectingAnAppEnab: Connecting an app enables its available tools, including write actions, within the permissions granted by that provider. Device tools follow the access configured on that computer. Your instructions may send messages, modify files, change records, execute commands or cause charges in a connected account. You are responsible for granting appropriate access and reviewing consequential results. Disconnecting or stopping work does not undo completed actions.
messages.marketing.trustPages.connectRelaysAuthor: Connect relays authorized tool requests to your devices and apps. Requested file contents, directory listings, browser information, command output and app data may pass through our hosted service to your selected AI client. Operational audit records store metadata such as tool name, device, status and time, rather than a full copy of tool arguments and output. Saved tasks and hosted conversations use separate storage described below, so metadata-only audit does not mean that all content stays on your computer.
messages.marketing.trustPages.connectUnlimitedIsA: Pro, formerly Connect Unlimited, is a plan for people who use their own AI client, such as ChatGPT, Claude or Codex. It has no monthly Connect call cap and includes the number of computers shown at checkout and in your billing settings. Each computer is authenticated separately and can be revoked at any time. Published fair-use protections still apply: rate limits, provider limits and at most {computerRegistrationsPerDay} new computer registrations per day. A registered computer is not the same as a running session: each computer runs work within its own capacity. Browser Companion installations are counted separately, up to {browserInstallations}. Like every account, it can use the one-time Arc trial when offered. Whether your plan also includes Arc-hosted AI and monthly Credits is part of the terms you purchased, shown at checkout and in your billing settings. When it does, the Credits for each paid month are added at the start of that month and expire at its end, including on a yearly plan. When it does not, the plan includes no Arc-hosted AI, Arc Chat, hosted planning, model allowances or monthly Credits beyond that trial. It never upgrades automatically. If the plan ends, is cancelled or is refunded, no computer is deleted or revoked, but only as many computers as your current plan allows stay active: the first ones in the order you choose on the Devices page. The others are paused: they stay paired but cannot connect or run tools, and they resume automatically when you subscribe again, up to the number of computers your plan includes. New registrations follow your current plan's limit.
messages.marketing.trustPages.doNotUseRemoteArcTo: Do not use Remote Arc to bypass authorization, compromise systems, send unlawful or abusive content, or interfere with other users. We may restrict access for abuse, security incidents, legal requirements or material violations. Integrations, models and quotas may change as providers and the service evolve. We will describe the applicable offering at purchase; an enterprise service commitment requires a separate agreement.
messages.marketing.trustPages.googleAppsBetaAppli: Google Apps Beta applications include your account email, the Google email you want to test, selected apps and a short purpose. They are stored in our private support inbox; the application text is encrypted and available to authorized administrators. Customer email uses Cloudflare Email Routing, and reviewed replies may use SendPulse. Applying or approving access does not automatically send an email. Do not submit passwords or private mail/file contents. Contact support@remotearc.app to update or delete your application.

messages.marketing.trustPages.weRecordALimitedSet: We record a limited set of sign-in, workspace navigation, device, task and payment-step events to diagnose failures and understand where a flow stops. These records can include your account identifier, random per-tab journey and request identifiers, outcome, safe error code, duration and time. Browser observations are separate from verified payment records. Diagnostic events have a 30-day retention target and are available only to authorized administrators. This event stream does not collect card details, form content, conversations, file contents, raw URLs, IP addresses or exception text.
messages.marketing.trustPages.weUseCloudflareToHo: We use Cloudflare to host the service and store service data, Google for account sign-in, and Stripe where billing is enabled. Connected apps and model providers process the information needed for the requests you authorize under their own terms and settings. Your external AI provider may retain the tool results returned to its chat. Processing may occur outside your country; we do not promise a particular storage region or that these third parties never retain data.
messages.marketing.trustPages.weUseCookiesAndBrow: We use cookies and browser storage for sign-in, security, language, theme and workspace preferences. Installing the web app does not grant additional account or device access. The displayed revision date identifies this policy version. Questions about this policy can be sent through Support or to support@remotearc.app.
messages.marketing.trustPages.weUseGoogleAccountD: We use Google account data only for the app features you authorize. Our use and sharing follow the Google API Services User Data Policy, including Limited Use. We do not sell this data, use it for advertising, or use it to train general AI models. Requested data can be sent to your chosen AI client or the model provider serving your Arc conversation, with your consent. Use AI services configured consistently with these restrictions. Background Google app-call contents expire after seven days, become unavailable for replay, and are removed by periodic cleanup. You can delete these contents earlier from the app account controls. Minimal outcome, idempotency and accounting records remain. Saved chats, tasks, memories and independent third-party copies have separate controls. Human access is limited to specific user-authorized support, security or legal needs.
messages.marketing.trustPages.weUseYourSignInIden: We use your sign-in identity, name, email address, account identifiers and session records to provide and secure your workspace. For paired computers, we store device names, platform information, credential hashes and connection timestamps. Raw device pairing credentials are not stored in the hosted database.

messages.marketing.trustPages.whereArcIsEnabledFo: Where Arc is enabled for your account, we store encrypted conversation content and saved work state so you can continue later. Tasks and routines can retain their objective, instructions, schedule, limits, progress, bounded tool observations, summaries and completion evidence. messages.marketing.trustPages.wherePaidPlansAreAv: Where paid plans are available, Stripe handles checkout and payment methods. messages.marketing.trustPages.youCanDisconnectApp: You can disconnect apps, revoke AI-client grants, and remove paired devices from your workspace.
